content_preview.title: pg_clickhouse v0.10 Pushes Correlated Subqueries to ClickHouse, Cutting a TPC-H Query From 32.7 Seconds to 37 Milliseconds
content_preview.summary: ClickHouse's pg_clickhouse extension now pushes whole correlated subqueries down to ClickHouse, taking TPC-H pushdown coverage from 12 to 16 of 22 queries.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

ClickHouse has released version 0.10.0 of pg_clickhouse, the PostgreSQL extension that lets a Postgres database offload analytic queries to a connected ClickHouse server, adding support for pushing whole correlated subqueries down to ClickHouse instead of evaluating them locally row by row. According to [ClickHouse's official blog](https://clickhouse.com/blog/pg_clickhouse-whats-new-july-2026), the change took one TPC-H benchmark query, Q17, from 32.7 seconds to 37 milliseconds, whi...

editor_notes.source_verification: Read both source snapshots in full from disk (gunzip'd, sha256 verified against manifest.json: source-0.html.gz = bb02ca5681ef6f319baab013aa8e03ed0288c9a8dfe70d60a6e942e2e1340e1f matches; source-1.html.gz = 8f1783bb5571e28601e6f849cb73702ee75218b6de36522003a34a7f2d06c5bc matches). source-0.html.gz (clickhouse.com blog, 'What's new in pg_clickhouse v0.10.0', Josh Ventura, Aug 11, 2026) supports every quoted claim verbatim, including: the headline benchmark ('back when it evaluated once per outer row against 6M line items at scale factor 1, took 32.7 seconds. Fully pushed down, it's 37 milliseconds. That's three orders of magnitude difference'), the full Q2/Q17/Q22 before/after table (Q2: 3,446ms->24ms; Q17: 32,709ms->37ms; Q22: 1,415ms->45ms), the native-Postgres comparison ('outperforms native PostgreSQL's own plan for the same query (2.1s)'), the pushdown scoreboard ('moved from 12 of 22 TPC-H queries fully pushed down to 16, leaving only 6 to go'), the December 2025 milestone ('moved the needle from 3 of 22 TPC-H queries all the way to 12'), the six remaining queries (Q13, Q15, Q16, Q18, Q20, Q21 - verbatim list match), the ClickHouse 25.8 version-gate language, the three-valued/two-valued NULL semantics passage, and the clickhouse_query/clickhouse_perform/clickhouse_raw_query function descriptions. source-1.html.gz (GitHub release page for v0.10.0) corroborates the Aug 11, 2026 release date ('11 Aug 14:41') and the subquery-pushdown release note. No WebFetch fallback was needed; both snapshots returned 200 and were fully readable.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Per the reviewer's specific instruction, I independently verified the 32.7s->37ms Q17 figure and the '12 to 16 of 22' coverage claim against the raw blog text rather than trusting the submission. Both trace verbatim to direct quotes/statements in the ClickHouse blog post, not to the bot's own arithmetic. One nuance worth noting for the record (not a bot error): the blog's own narrative is internally slightly loose — it describes the scoreboard moving from 12 to 16 (a delta of 4) but only names and charts three specific newly-pushed queries (Q2, Q17, Q22) as 'Three more TPC-H queries now fully push down.' The GitHub release notes separately mention Q11 among the shapes covered by this release, which plausibly accounts for the fourth. The article faithfully reproduces the blog's own framing on both counts without resolving or obscuring this; it does not fabricate a fourth query or claim the three named queries are the complete set behind the 12->16 delta. This is a pre-existing ambiguity in the primary source, not a submission defect, and does not affect the headline/lead's core, precisely-sourced claim.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual throughout. No editorializing, no AI self-reference, no sensationalized language beyond directly-quoted material from the source itself (e.g. 'the trophy').
